name: K–5 visual art across grade bands

input.topic: Explore balance, repetition, rhythm, color, symbolism, and theme through modern portrait design. Picasso may be one reference, but students should make original choices rather than copy an artist's style.
input.objective: Students will use visual elements intentionally and explain at least one artistic choice at an age-appropriate level.
input.student_needs: Some younger students need oral directions and simple choices; older students are ready for symbolism, mood, and critique. Several students benefit from visual examples and reduced fine-motor complexity.

constraints.space_constraints: Students work at shared tables in an art room used by the next class immediately afterward.
must_avoid: requiring every grade to complete the same cognitive task
constraints.other: Identify what is essential before class versus optional if time allows.

input.additional_notes: The teacher teaches a different grade each period and needs grade-band adaptations that preserve one central concept.

name: Kindergarten story sequencing through purposeful play

input.topic: Retell a familiar story in sequence using oral language, movement, and simple props.
input.objective: Students will orally retell beginning, middle, and end and place three events in order.
input.student_needs: Several students are emerging multilingual learners, four students are reluctant to speak in the whole group, and the class benefits from movement every 8 to 10 minutes.

constraints.space_constraints: Small carpet area with tables around the perimeter.
constraints.other: Play should produce evidence of sequencing, not just fill time.

input.topic: Decode and spell words with vowel teams ai and ay.
input.objective: Students will read and spell one-syllable words containing ai or ay and explain where each spelling usually appears.
input.student_needs: Six students still need sound-by-sound blending support; five are ready to apply the pattern in sentences; several need frequent response opportunities.

must_avoid: silent independent work longer than 7 minutes
constraints.other: The teacher cannot run three elaborate stations.

input.topic: Compare fractions with the same numerator or denominator using visual models and reasoning.
input.objective: Students will compare two fractions and justify the comparison with a drawing or concrete model.
input.student_needs: About one third of the class confuses numerator and denominator; several students finish quickly and need reasoning challenges rather than more computation.

constraints.space_constraints: Desks are in tight rows and cannot be moved.
must_avoid: assuming students already know cross multiplication
constraints.other: Use the limited fraction strips without creating a materials bottleneck.

input.topic: Use evidence to explain how water changes land through weathering and erosion.
input.objective: Students will distinguish weathering from erosion and construct an evidence-based explanation from observable examples.
input.student_needs: Several students need vocabulary support and sentence frames; the class can discuss evidence but tends to jump to claims without explaining reasoning.

must_avoid: inventing a hands-on lab without materials
constraints.other: Keep the work scientifically accurate and intellectually active without pretending a demonstration occurred.

name: Grade 6 social studies with meaningful integration

input.topic: Explain how river geography shaped settlement and trade in early civilizations.
input.objective: Students will make and defend a causal claim connecting river geography to one settlement or trade decision.
input.student_needs: Students can locate rivers but need support moving from map observations to causal explanations. Reading levels vary widely.

must_avoid: writing unrelated paragraphs just to claim ELA integration
constraints.other: Any math, ELA, or art connection must deepen the geographic reasoning rather than become an add-on.

input.topic: Choose the strongest evidence for an argument and explain why it supports the claim.
input.objective: Students will select relevant evidence and write or orally rehearse reasoning that connects it to a claim.
input.student_needs: Many students can quote text but struggle to explain relevance. Four students need a reduced writing load while preserving the reasoning goal.

constraints.space_constraints: Students must remain seated because another class is testing next door.
must_avoid: lowering the reasoning demand for students who write less
constraints.other: The class has low energy immediately after lunch.

input.topic: Compose, perform, and revise an eight-beat rhythm using quarter notes, paired eighth notes, and rests.
input.objective: Students will create and perform an eight-beat rhythm, listen for accuracy, and revise one choice based on feedback.
input.student_needs: Several students need a visual beat grid; some are uncomfortable performing alone; advanced students need a musical challenge that still fits eight beats.

constraints.space_constraints: Music room with chairs in a semicircle and no room for large-group movement.
constraints.other: Noise rises quickly during instrument distribution.

name: Grade 8 PE in a shared gym

input.topic: Use spacing, communication, and support to maintain possession in a small-sided invasion game.
input.objective: Students will create passing options off the ball and use specific communication during small-sided play.
input.student_needs: The class includes students with varied mobility and endurance; several students avoid competitive play; directions need to be brief and visible through demonstration.

constraints.space_constraints: Half of a gym shared with another class; no wall space and noise is high.
must_avoid: assuming every student moves in the same way

name: High school biology with no lab setup

input.topic: Predict and explain passive transport across a cell membrane using concentration gradients.
input.objective: Students will predict the net movement of particles in unfamiliar scenarios and justify each prediction using concentration gradient and equilibrium.
input.student_needs: Students know the vocabulary but often reverse the direction of net movement. Several benefit from diagrams before symbolic explanations.

must_avoid: water-channel analogies that create scientific misconceptions
constraints.other: The final check must reveal whether students can transfer the idea to a new scenario.
